Methodology & Data Sources

How your shrinkage exposure is calculated — and why the numbers are accurate

Every figure in this calculator is derived from published industry data, calibrated against A-Z Global field experience across 40+ DACH and Gulf retail engagements. This page explains exactly where each number comes from and what it means for your operation.

Step-by-Step Calculation
1
Baseline Shrinkage Rate
We apply your country and sector-specific shrinkage benchmark as a percentage of net sales. These rates come from the EHI Inventurdifferenzen Report 2025 (DACH), ECR Europe Loss Prevention Report 2024 (Pan-European), and Oliver Wyman GCC Retail Security Index (Gulf). Rates range from 0.42% (Swiss grocery) to 2.8% (UAE electronics) — and are updated annually.
Annual Loss = Annual Revenue × Shrinkage Rate
2
Stock Count Overrun (SCO)
Stock count overrun represents the hidden cost of inventory inaccuracy — the time and labour your team spends on recounts, reconciliation, and investigation when stock counts do not match system records. SCO is distinct from shrinkage: it is an operational inefficiency cost, not a theft figure. The default SCO cost per location is €1,200–€4,500 annually depending on operation size and frequency.
SCO Cost = SCO Value per Location × Number of Locations
3
Margin-Adjusted Loss
Shrinkage hits at cost price — but its impact is felt at the margin level. To recover €10,000 of shrinkage loss at a 35% gross margin, a retailer must generate €28,571 of additional sales. The calculator converts your raw loss figure into the equivalent additional revenue you would need to generate to offset it — making the true business impact visible.
Revenue Needed to Offset = Annual Loss ÷ Gross Margin %
4
Recovery Potential
Not all shrinkage is recoverable — but a professionally implemented loss prevention programme consistently achieves 25–40% shrinkage reduction within 12 months. The calculator uses a conservative 30% recovery rate as the default, derived from A-Z Global field data across 40+ European and Gulf retail engagements. This figure is intentionally conservative: it reflects programmes that are implemented competently but not yet at full maturity.
Recoverable Loss = Annual Loss × Recovery Rate (30%)
5
Return on Investment
The ROI calculation compares the recoverable loss against a typical professional loss prevention investment. For a 10-store fashion retailer with €30M annual turnover, the average annual LP programme cost (technology, training, audit, consulting) is €45,000–€95,000. The recoverable shrinkage at 30% recovery typically exceeds this investment by 3–8×, giving an ROI of 300–800% in year one.
ROI = (Recoverable Loss − LP Investment) ÷ LP Investment × 100%
Shrinkage Benchmarks by Region & Sector

The benchmark rates in this calculator are sourced from three primary datasets, updated annually. We do not use industry averages — we use country and sector-specific rates that reflect the actual risk profile of your operation.

🇩🇪
EHI Retail Institute
Inventurdifferenzen 2025
Germany, Austria, Switzerland. The definitive DACH shrinkage dataset covering 350+ retailers across all major sectors. Published annually by the European retail research institute.
Fashion: 0.8–1.4% · Grocery: 0.45–0.7% · Electronics: 0.9–1.6%
🇪🇺
ECR Europe
Loss Prevention Report 2024
Pan-European shrinkage data covering 14 countries. The ECR dataset is the most comprehensive European benchmark, covering all major retail sectors with country-level granularity.
UK: 1.1–1.9% · France: 0.95–1.5% · Netherlands: 0.7–1.2%
🌍
Oliver Wyman
GCC Retail Security Index
Gulf Cooperation Council retail benchmarks covering UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. The only published dataset with GCC-specific shrinkage rates by sector.
UAE: 1.2–2.8% · KSA: 1.0–2.2% · Qatar: 0.9–1.8%
What This Tool Does Not Include — and Why

To keep the output credible and conservative, we deliberately exclude several loss categories that would make the figures significantly larger:

❌ Administrative errors
Pricing errors, receiving discrepancies, and paperwork mistakes typically add 15–25% to total shrinkage. Not included because they require operational audit data to quantify accurately.
❌ Supplier fraud
Short deliveries, invoice manipulation, and collusion with receiving staff. ECR Europe estimates this at 0.1–0.3% of revenue in DACH — excluded from the baseline calculation.
❌ Reputational and insurance costs
Repeat victimisation leads to higher insurance premiums and brand damage in affected locations. Not quantified here but significant for luxury and premium sectors.
❌ Staff replacement costs from theft-related terminations
Average DACH retail staff replacement cost is €8,000–€15,000 per incident including recruitment, training, and productivity loss during the transition period.
The total financial impact of inadequate security in a retail operation is consistently 1.4–1.8× the headline shrinkage figure when all cost categories are included. Our calculator shows you the minimum.

Article 3

Legal Basis for Processing — GDPR Article 6

We process your personal data only where we have a valid legal basis under GDPR Article 6. Different processing activities rely on different bases as set out below.

Art. 6(1)(a) — Consent
Marketing communications
Sending you the audit results email, follow-up analysis emails, and consultation invitation. You provide consent via the checkbox on the audit submission form. You may withdraw consent at any time by clicking unsubscribe or emailing privacy@a-zglobal.com.
Art. 6(1)(b) — Contract
Delivering audit results
Processing your audit answers and generating your personalised risk report constitutes performance of the service you have requested. This processing is necessary to deliver what you asked for when completing the audit.
Art. 6(1)(f) — Legitimate Interests
Internal analysis and service improvement
Analysing aggregate (anonymised) audit response patterns to improve question quality and benchmark accuracy. Our legitimate interest is improving the quality of our security advisory tools. This processing never uses your personal data in identifiable form.
Art. 6(1)(c) — Legal Obligation
Record keeping
Retaining records of client engagements for the duration required by applicable commercial and tax law in Germany (typically 6–10 years for business records). This applies only to confirmed client relationships, not leads.

Article 10

Data Security

We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect your personal data against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction, in accordance with GDPR Article 32.

Processing your audit answers and generating your personalised risk report constitutes performance of the service you have requested. This processing is necessary to deliver what you asked for when completing the audit.

Analysing aggregate (anonymised) audit response patterns to improve question quality and benchmark accuracy. Our legitimate interest is improving the quality of our security advisory tools. This processing never uses your personal data in identifiable form.
Art. 6(1)(c) — Legal Obligation
Record keeping
Retaining records of client engagements for the duration required by applicable commercial and tax law in Germany (typically 6–10 years for business records). This applies only to confirmed client relationships, not leads.
